relations.subject: Takakusu Junjirō
relations.evidence: After primary school, he studied at the leading Jōdo Shinshū educational institution, today's Ryūkoku University, from 1885 to 1889

relations.subject: Takakusu Junjirō
relations.evidence: Through the introduction of the Jōdo Shinshū cleric NANJO BUN’YŪ, Takakusu was able to study Indology under FRIEDRICH MAX MÜLLER (1823–1900) at Oxford

relations.subject: Takakusu Junjirō
relations.evidence: While at Oxford, he assisted Müller with the Sacred Books of the East project.

relations.subject: Takakusu Junjirō
relations.evidence: Takakusu also studied in Paris with SYLVAIN LÉVI

relations.subject: Takakusu Junjirō
relations.evidence: SYLVAIN LÉVI, with whom he would later collaborate on the Hōbōgirin Buddhist encyclopedia project.

relations.subject: Takakusu Junjirō
relations.evidence: He returned to Japan in 1897 to lecture in Indian philosophy at Tokyo Imperial University, where he served as professor from 1899 to 1927, being appointed to the chair of Sanskrit studies in 1901.

relations.subject: Takakusu Junjirō
relations.evidence: in 1906 was a founding member of the Japanese Esperantists Association.
